full_judgment: 12. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, learned counsel for the defendant-respondent, has argued that the plaintiffs have not raised any issue as to the sending of rent by money order and there being no dispute that the rent is being deposited in the name of the plaintiffs in Misc. Case No. 202/82, it must be presumed that the proceedings there have been regularly taken, that is, the deposit must have been made after remittance of the rent by money order. It is difficult to accept the submission of Mr. Hossain because of the heavy burden that lies upon the tenant to discharge. The onus is upon the tenant to prove that the conditions for depositing the rent with the Rent Controller were satisfied. It is not enough to prove that the rent was deposited under section 19 without further proof that the tenant was legally entitled to make the deposit. There cannot be any presumption as to due offer of rent to the landlord nor the landlord is required to raise the issue of money order, etc. As stated in the 29 DLR (SC) 13 case, no duty under the law has been cast upon the landlord to pursue the tenant in demanding the rent which falls due. It is rather the duty of the tenant to pay rent to the landlord in time with a view to saving him from being a defaulter, the consequence of which is his eviction from the premises in his occupation.
